answeredFailures: BLOCKING 1: the memory paragraph cited /sys/fs/cgroup/memory.current, a file no role container of this pod has. The tester is right and the defect is mine: my command was `cat /sys/fs/cgroup/memory.current 2>/dev/null || cat /sys/fs/cgroup/memory/memory.usage_in_bytes`, the fallback fired silently, and I wrote the first path beside a number the second produced. Fixed at bae04203582d38b8c4a8384c1144639d50ca6317: memory.current and cgroup v2 are gone from the note entirely — a path that cannot be run here does not go in it — and where a counter is named it is the v1 path /sys/fs/cgroup/memory/memory.usage_in_bytes, with `ls /sys/fs/cgroup` given as how a reader sees which layout their own container has.

BLOCKING 2: the paragraph asserted per-container charging on a counter that is the gVisor sandbox's. What the pod does show carries the warning: a dd bs=1M count=100 into /var/run/legion/private moves free -k's shared from 132 to 102,532 KiB and releases it on removal.

The golden-fixture citation is dropped from that sentence, since the fixture names no ServiceAccount only because its operator config sets none.

Not asked for and not done: nothing was added that this round did not run. The architect's standing instruction, if this paragraph fails again, is to cut it to the free -k sentence plus one attributed clause and drop every counter, path and figure.

Also in this round, after the architect corrected a figure it had given me: the limits sentence could be read as one 1Gi shared by three roles. Each role container has a memory limit of its own and they differ — request equal to limit, 1Gi for the architect, planner and merger, 4Gi for the reviewer, 6Gi for the implementer and tester (verified in the golden pod JSON) — and the note now says so and marks the numbers as the pod spec's rather than anything a container can read.
